newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end near session lows in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end near session lows in slow trade.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended near session lows Wednesday, as most traders left the market early ahead of a long holiday weekend, sources said.
January finished 8.4 cents lower at $3.497 per million British thermal units. February settled down 6.1 cents at $3.056, while other '97 months were a half-cent to two cents lower.
"I'd rather by flat to long than short," one trader said, adding he expected hefty storage withdrawals in December.
NYMEX will be closed on Thursday and Friday for the Thanksgiving holiday.
Support in January was still in the mid-$3.40s, then around $3.34. Resistance was seen in the $3.59-3.60 area, then the $3.68 contract high.
NYMEX said an estimated 13,493 Hub contracts traded, down sharply from Tuesday's revised tally of 23,724.
In the cash market, November prices on the Gulf Coast pipes were about 15 cents lower in the mid-$3.70s to low-$3.80s, while the Midcontinent market hovered in the low-to-mid $3.60s.
NYMEX Alberta natgas remained untraded today but January settled off 35 cents at $1.60.
Cash prices for November remained flat in the mid-C$1.90s per gigajoule, or the mid-$1.50s per mmBtu.
NYMEX Permian natgas also was untraded but January settled 10 cents lower at $3.05.
Permian cash prices for the remainder of November softened by more than five cents to the $3.50-3.55 range.

In congruence with NYMEX, KCBT's January contract finished six cents lower at $3.31, while Feb was down five cents at $2.86 at the close. The East/West spread narrowed slightly to 18.7 cents (NYMEX premium).
Waha prices for the rest of November ranged anywhere from $3.55 to $3.65, traders said, still carrying about a 30-cent premium to January futures.
